title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1968-10-12
lineage: SBD > MR > DAT > Sonic Solutions > EAC > CoolEdit > CD

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of the Avalon Ballroom 10‑12‑68 show delivers a blistering Other One suite, monster Eleven and soaring Dark Star.
ai_review.review: This recording presents an exceptionally energetic 1968 Dead performance – the Other One/cryptical sequence erupts with tribal power, The Eleven is repeatedly called “the best ever,” and Dark Star soars on Jerry’s incendiary guitar.  The soundboard source is praised as crystal‑clear, buttery and superb (with only a minor shakers‑too‑loud complaint), making the show instantly listenable from start to finish.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 100 reviews, virtually all five‑star, uniformly praising both musical performance and audio fidelity; the few minor criticisms are negligible.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crystal‑clear, buttery mix with superb instrument separation; a couple of reviewers note shakers in Dark Star a bit loud and some missing banter, but overall the recording is considered one of the best‑sounding ’68 soundboards.

standout_songs: The Other One (cryptical → other one suite)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A ferocious first set that builds into a massive Dark Star, followed by a second set where the cryptical→Other One suite and The Eleven dominate; transitions (drums‑jam‑feedback) are highlighted as seamless and the overall pacing is described as nonstop fire.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar tone and solos on Dark Star and The Other One are called “ripping,” “blazing,” and “perfect”; vocal delivery on Death Don't Have No Mercy praised as powerful.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass solo in The Eleven described as thunderous; overall bass work noted as tight and driving the jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals on several numbers (Death Don't Have No Mercy, New Potato Caboose) are highlighted as strong; some mention of early Phil singing on That’s It for The Other One chorus.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keyboard/organ absent – reviewers note the lack of Pigpen/organ but it doesn’t diminish the show; no specific praise for keyboards because they’re missing.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming praised, especially the drums‑jam‑feedback segment; percussion energy described as “wild” and “extraterrestrial.”
